_about: One shared moment of the product. Every design direction draws exactly this moment so the directions can be compared side by side. Names, labels and field shapes come from the product's own demo seeds (frontend/src/data.ts) and from the real API shapes; nothing here is live personal data. Keys starting with _ are notes for designers, not content.

now._note: The interface ships in English and Romanian. Draw it in English, but the owner writes to it in either language (see the conversation) and Romanian diacritics (ă â î ș ț) must render in your fonts.

product.name: Nerva
product.one_sentence: A private AI that works while you sleep and is owned by the person it serves.
product.what_it_is: A local-first personal assistant: one orchestrator (Jarvis) and 17 specialist agents running on the owner's own workstation and GPU. It works proactively, and anything risky waits for the owner's decision.

navigation._note: Today: 16 rail modes + a hidden 'Console' overlay with 137 panels + three loose buttons. The code's own structure supports nine areas; the 137 panels become second-level pages of these areas and must all be reachable by search. You may rename or reorder, but every area needs a home.

areas.holds: conversation with the orchestrator, what needs you, what happened, today

areas.label: Work
areas.holds: decisions, missions, projects board, scheduled jobs, sessions, activity

areas.label: Agents
areas.holds: the 18 agents, their homes (finance, health, family, knowledge), personas

areas.label: Trust
areas.holds: audit chain, emergency stop, capabilities, permissions, payments, secrets

areas.label: Build
areas.holds: skills, workflows, sandbox, images, creative tools

areas.label: Connect
areas.holds: channels, integrations, MCP servers, webhooks, rooms

areas.label: Observe

areas.label: Settings
areas.holds: models and backends, appearance, backup, updates

global: Search and command (Ctrl+K) — finds every area, panel, agent and action

health._note: Today the product has no single verdict: it shows seven badges, a marquee and five meter rows, plus a hard-coded 'ALL NOMINAL'. Design ONE honest verdict with its causes. 'Unknown' and 'stale' are real states and must look different from 'ok'.
health.headline: Working, with 4 local services down

causes.impact: Not blocking: the model is being served by Ollama instead.
Long-term recall is using the built-in vector store.
The knowledge graph is running in memory only.

facts._note: The hub counts which route each run used; it is not a verified network measurement. Show the basis next to the number. When it is only derived from the strict-local switch say 'derived'; when unknown say 'unknown'.

facts.value: Sealed — nothing can leave this machine
other_values: Hybrid — a cloud route is reachable

facts.value: 2 of 2 running · 1 session in the last 15 min

facts._note: Not measured by the hub yet. Show unknown as unknown, never as 0.

meters.label: VRAM
meters._note: Expected while a 31B model is loaded; high VRAM is why the interface must stay light on the GPU.

autonomy._note: The approval mode is global, with per-agent overrides. It is one of three values and should be visible wherever decisions or the composer are.

modes.label: Auto
modes.meaning: Safe and reversible actions run on their own; risky ones wait.

modes.label: Ask
modes.meaning: Anything with a side effect waits for you.

modes.label: Off
modes.meaning: Agents may read and think, nothing acts.

autonomy._interrupts_note: The product budgets how often it may interrupt the owner (4 a day).

risk_tiers._note: Four tiers decided by the hub in code. Friction must follow the tier. Today the interface collapses them into 'reversible / irreversible' and shows the same small red pill on every card.

tiers.name: Read only
tiers.friction: none — recorded in the audit chain

tiers.name: External — reaches someone or something outside
tiers.friction: two steps: review what will be sent, then confirm

rules: No keyboard shortcut may approve or reject. This is a deliberate safety rule of the product; search and navigation may be keyboard-first, verdicts are not.
A control on the main screen must never pretend to decide. Approve / Reject / Defer must be the real thing or absent.
The emergency stop is deliberately one click and must be reachable from the home screen.

decisions._note: This is the queue the owner acts on. 18 raw requests are waiting; many are repeats raised by the health observer, and the hub already groups them. Draw the grouped view: 9 actions in 6 groups. Actions available on every request: Approve, Edit then approve, Reject (optional reason), Defer, and Preview (a dry run of what would execute).

conversation._note: The owner talks to Jarvis; Jarvis routes to specialists. Replies render Markdown. Draw the thread below, ending with a reply that is still streaming. Each reply carries provenance (which model, where it ran).

turns.text: Morning Jarvis — what does my day look like?
Good morning, Andrei. Three meetings today; the Raiffeisen review at 14:00 is the one that matters. Pepper holds your calendar, Stark prepped the KPI deltas. Weather is clear — good day to cycle in.
Stark pulled the numbers — **Digitaholic MRR is +6.2% WoW**; I flagged the missing churn-cohort slide for the review.
Gecko's watching the markets — EUR/RON steady at 4.97; idle cash is **€4.2k over buffer**, sweep available.
turns.waits_for_you: 1 action waits for your decision — Sweep €4,200 to the savings ladder

turns.text: Ce proiecte sunt de terminat acum?

turns.text_so_far: Trei proiecte au termene săptămâna aceasta: prezentarea pentru Raiffeisen (azi, 14:00), raportul lunar Digitaholic și

conversation._actions_note: Today each reply shows up to eight always-visible buttons (Photoshop, Save to Obsidian, Create task, Teach skill, Download Word …). Decide what is always visible and what lives behind 'More'.

composer._note: Today: a single-line input wrapped in four always-visible rows with about 14 controls and two help sentences. It should be a multi-line box with progressive disclosure. It must show who will receive the message and the autonomy mode.

agents._note: 18 agents in four tiers. The current screen lists all 18 twice (a roster column and a decorative node graph). Research says: show agents by exception — working, waiting on you, just finished — and collapse the rest into a count. Today's hub only reports 'ready' or 'idle'; richer states are the design intent, and 'idle' must still look right.
